title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Video2DoorTraversal: Real‑to‑Sim‑to‑Real Door Opening

### The Breakthrough
Video2DoorTraversal builds a simulation‑ready door model from a single RGB video (DoorTwin) and trains a dual‑depth policy (ArticuACT) that predicts coordinated base, arm, and gripper commands, achieving 96.57% success on five real doors and 80.95% zero‑shot success on unseen doors in about 13 seconds.

### The Caveats
The work reports high door‑opening success yet does not compare against any existing baselines, so its claimed superiority remains unverified.

## DECOWAM: Whole‑Body Coordination for Legged Manipulators

### The Breakthrough
DECOWAM freezes an adapted FastWAM backbone, adds lightweight residual adapters, a future‑bottleneck action predictor, and adversarially separates base/arm latent spaces with velocity conditioning, reducing action MSE by 21.7% (using only 25.95 M trainable parameters) and delivering the highest whole‑body coordination in 79 closed‑loop trials on the ARMDOG real‑robot dataset.

### The Caveats
The reported gains are demonstrated only on the ARMDOG dataset and a single legged robot, with no tests on other morphologies, terrains, or unseen environments, so it’s unclear whether the improvements generalize.

## Evidence‑Gated TAMP with Vision‑Language Models

### The Breakthrough
The Evidence Acquisition and Feasibility Gating (EAFG) framework generates exploratory subgoals via a vision‑language model, executes them with a task‑and‑motion‑planning engine, and applies a feasibility gate to ensure sufficient visual evidence before committing to a long‑horizon manipulation plan, reducing failures from missing or ambiguous objects.

### The Caveats
The paper reports higher task completion rates but provides no comparison against any established TAMP or vision‑language baselines, so the claimed improvement is unsubstantiated.

## Hierarchical RL for Dynamic Quadruped Jumping

### The Breakthrough
A hierarchical reinforcement‑learning system combines imitation‑learned low‑level locomotion skills with a vision‑aware high‑level planner that selects collision‑free maneuvers, enabling a quadruped to perform aerial‑style gate‑crossing jumps and to retarget the same pipeline to other high‑speed tasks without redesign.

### The Caveats
The paper presents no real‑world hardware tests or quantitative metrics, so the claimed high‑speed gate‑crossing agility remains unverified.

## Peppy: Simplified Robotics Framework for Non‑Robotics Developers

### The Breakthrough
Peppy orchestrates multiple simulation and control nodes via a lightweight daemon, using Apptainer containers to encapsulate MuJoCo and related services; a single launch command builds eight instances across six node types and exposes a web UI for teleoperation, scripted actions, gestures, and motor health views, abstracting away robotics‑specific setup.

### The Caveats
The demo never validates the stack on actual robot hardware, so its claimed ease‑of‑use and robustness remain unproven outside simulation.

## Synaptic Harmony: Multi‑Agent Q‑Learning Swarm Foraging Simulation

### The Breakthrough
The repository provides a configurable Python sandbox where each forager maintains an independent NumPy‑based Q‑table, enabling fully distributed Q‑learning with epsilon‑greedy exploration and decaying rates in a renewable‑resource grid world with moving obstacles, all rendered in real‑time and logged for reproducibility.

### The Caveats
The repository offers no quantitative comparison to any existing multi‑agent foraging algorithms, so the claimed emergent cooperation remains unvalidated against established baselines.

### Priority
Video2DoorTraversal is the most impactful today because it delivers a high‑success, low‑cost sim‑to‑real door‑opening pipeline that works on real wheel‑legged robots, demonstrating a clear path from perception to embodied action.

### One action
Reproduce the DoorTwin pipeline on a single RGB video of a door you have access to, then run the generated ArticuACT policy in simulation to verify its performance before attempting real‑world deployment.

### What to watch
Four of the stories push embodied AI forward through different lenses: Door traversal showcases perception‑driven sim‑to‑real pipelines for long‑horizon loco‑manipulation; DECOWAM advances whole‑body coordination for legged manipulators via lightweight adapters; Evidence‑Gated TAMP leverages vision‑language models to gather visual evidence before planning; and the quadruped work targets aggressive dynamic locomotion using hierarchical RL. Together they signal a trend toward integrating vision, language, and learned primitives to broaden robot capabilities across hardware platforms.
